ℝ^p = Eucl p; cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1} for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^m; ι(v) := cons(0, v) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι∘v := (fun i => ι (v i)) and (e₀, ι∘v) := Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι (v i)) for tuples v; D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, M := mass; for a test form ω, ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl p) q) x; Dψ(y) := fderiv ℝ ψ y; dω denotes the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ q ω, which is definitionally exteriorDerivative ω = extDeriv ω.

1. (Preliminaries.) (i) As in the construction of ι: w ↦ Fin.cons 0 w is ℝ-linear (coordinatewise with Fin.cases), so ι is a continuous linear map ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ^{m+1} with ι(v) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) definitionally. (ii) For fixed s, cons(s, x) = cons(s, 0) + ι(x) (apply EuclideanSpace.equiv and compare coordinates by Fin.cases), so x ↦ cons(s, x) has derivative ι at every x (HasFDerivAt.const_add of ι.hasFDerivAt). (iii) The underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n ω is exteriorDerivative ω = extDeriv ω (definitional; use `show`). (iv) Test forms are C^∞, hence differentiable at every point (ContDiff.differentiable). (v) exteriorDerivative_apply: for ω differentiable at y and u : Fin (n+1) → E, dω(y)(u) = Σ_{i : Fin (n+1)} (−1)^i • fderiv ℝ (fun z => ω z (i.removeNth u)) y (u i). (vi) For ω differentiable at y, a constant tuple u and a vector h: fderiv ℝ (fun z => ω z u) y h = (Dω(y) h)(u) (fderiv_continuousAlternatingMap_apply_const_apply).
2. ((E0).) Let ψ ∈ D^0(ℝ^{m+1}), y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, v : Fin 0 → ℝ^m and u := Fin.cons e₀ (ι∘v) : Fin 1 → ℝ^{m+1}. By (v) and Fin.sum_univ_one, dψ(y)(u) = (−1)^0 • fderiv ℝ (fun z => ψ z (removeNth 0 u)) y (u 0) = (Dψ(y)(e₀))(removeNth 0 u) by (vi) and Fin.cons_zero. Both removeNth 0 u and ι∘v are functions on the empty type Fin 0, hence equal; so dψ(y)(e₀, ι∘v) = Dψ(y)(e₀)(ι∘v).
3. ((E1), expansion of dψ.) Let ψ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), φ ∈ D^j(ℝ^m) and s with φ(x)(w) = ψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘w) for all x, w. Fix x, v : Fin (j+1) → ℝ^m, put y := cons(s,x) and u := Fin.cons e₀ (ι∘v) : Fin (j+2) → ℝ^{m+1}. By (v) and Fin.sum_univ_succ,
   dψ(y)(u) = fderiv ℝ (fun z => ψ z (removeNth 0 u)) y (u 0) + Σ_{l : Fin (j+1)} (−1)^{l+1} • fderiv ℝ (fun z => ψ z (removeNth l.succ u)) y (u l.succ).
   Here removeNth 0 u = Fin.tail u = ι∘v (Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons), u 0 = e₀ (Fin.cons_zero), u l.succ = ι(v l) (Fin.cons_succ), and removeNth l.succ u = u ∘ (l.succ).succAbove = Fin.cons e₀ (l.removeNth (ι∘v)) (Fin.cons_comp_succ_succAbove) = Fin.cons e₀ (ι ∘ (l.removeNth v)) (Fin.removeNth is precomposition with succAbove). With (vi) the first term is Dψ(y)(e₀)(ι∘v) and the l-th term of the sum is (−1)^{l+1}·Dψ(y)(ι(v l))(e₀, ι∘(l.removeNth v)).
4. ((E1), expansion of dφ.) By (v) for φ at x, dφ(x)(v) = Σ_{l : Fin (j+1)} (−1)^l • fderiv ℝ (fun x′ => φ x′ (l.removeNth v)) x (v l). For every w : Fin j → ℝ^m the hypothesis says that, as functions on all of ℝ^m, (fun x′ => φ x′ w) = (fun z => ψ z (e₀, ι∘w)) ∘ (x′ ↦ cons(s,x′)). By the chain rule ((vi)'s HasFDerivAt.continuousAlternatingMap_apply_const composed with (ii)), fderiv ℝ (fun x′ => φ x′ w) x = (fderiv ℝ (fun z => ψ z (e₀, ι∘w)) y) ∘L ι, whose value at v l is, by (vi), Dψ(y)(ι(v l))(e₀, ι∘w). With w := l.removeNth v, the l-th term of dφ(x)(v) is (−1)^l·Dψ(y)(ι(v l))(e₀, ι∘(l.removeNth v)).
5. (Comparison.) (−1)^{l+1} = −(−1)^l (Fin.val_succ, pow_succ, mul_neg_one, neg_smul), so the sum in step 3 equals −dφ(x)(v) term by term (Finset.sum_congr, Finset.sum_neg_distrib). Therefore dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v) = Dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀)(ι∘v) − dφ(x)(v). ∎

Notation. ℝ^p = Eucl p; ι(v) := cons(0, v) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι∘v := (fun i => ι (v i)) and (e₀, ι∘v) := Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι (v i)) for tuples v; b^{(p)}_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ i (= EuclideanSpace.single i 1); for a q-covector γ on ℝ^p (γ : Covector (Eucl p) q), |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ = (Σ_{I : Fin q → Fin p strictly increasing} γ(b_{I 0}, …, b_{I (q−1)})²)^{1/2} with b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ i, and ‖γ‖ is its operator norm.

1. (Basis vectors.) e₀ = b^{(m+1)}_0, because EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply gives b^{(m+1)}_0 = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1. For j : Fin m, ι(b^{(m)}_j) = b^{(m+1)}_{j.succ}: apply the injective map EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ to both sides (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply) and compare coordinates by Fin.cases: at coordinate 0 the left side is Fin.cons 0 _ 0 = 0 and the right side is (single j.succ 1) 0 = 0 since j.succ ≠ 0; at coordinate i.succ the left side is (single j 1) i and the right side is (single j.succ 1) i.succ, which agree because Fin.succ is injective.
2. (Sums along an injection.) Let A, B be finite types, g : A → B injective, F : B → ℝ with F ≥ 0 and G : A → ℝ with G(a) ≤ F(g(a)) for all a. Then Σ_a G(a) ≤ Σ_a F(g(a)) (Finset.sum_le_sum) = Σ_{b ∈ g(A)} F(b) (Finset.sum_image, using injectivity) ≤ Σ_b F(b) (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg, F ≥ 0).
3. ((C1).) Let γ, γ′ be as in (C1). Unfolding covectorEuclideanNorm, |γ′| = √S′ and |γ| = √S with S′ := Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin m} G(I), G(I) := (if I strictly increasing then γ′(b^{(m)} ∘ I)² else 0), and S := Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin (m+1)} F(J), F(J) := (if J strictly increasing then γ(b^{(m+1)} ∘ J)² else 0) ≥ 0. As √ is monotone (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt) it suffices to show S′ ≤ S, which follows from step 2 with g(I) := Fin.cons 0 (fun i => (I i).succ) once we check:
   (a) g is injective: if g(I) = g(I′), evaluating at i.succ gives (I i).succ = (I′ i).succ, hence I i = I′ i for all i.
   (b) If I is strictly increasing, so is g(I): let a < b in Fin (k+1) and use Fin.cases on a and b. If a = 0 = b this contradicts a < b. If a = 0 and b = j.succ, then g(I)(a) = 0 < (I j).succ = g(I)(b) (Fin.succ_pos). If a = i.succ and b = 0, a < b is impossible (Fin.not_lt_zero). If a = i.succ and b = j.succ, then i < j (Fin.succ_lt_succ_iff), so I i < I j and (I i).succ < (I j).succ.
   (c) G(I) ≤ F(g(I)) for every I: if I is not strictly increasing, G(I) = 0 ≤ F(g(I)). Otherwise both `if`s take their first branch by (b), and by the hypothesis on γ′, γ′(b^{(m)} ∘ I) = γ(Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι(b^{(m)}_{I i}))); by Fin.cases and step 1 (index 0: e₀ = b^{(m+1)}_0; index i.succ: ι(b^{(m)}_{I i}) = b^{(m+1)}_{(I i).succ}) this tuple equals b^{(m+1)} ∘ g(I). Hence G(I) = F(g(I)).
   So S′ ≤ S and |γ′| ≤ |γ|.
4. ((C2).) Identical, with A := (Fin q → Fin m), B := (Fin q → Fin (m+1)), g(I) := fun i => (I i).succ (injective because Fin.succ is injective; strictly increasing whenever I is, by Fin.succ_lt_succ_iff), and γ′(b^{(m)} ∘ I) = γ(fun i => ι(b^{(m)}_{I i})) = γ(b^{(m+1)} ∘ g(I)) by the hypothesis and step 1.
5. ((C3).) For every I : Fin n → Fin P, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm gives |α(b ∘ I)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i ‖b_{I i}‖ = ‖α‖, the basis vectors having norm 1 (OrthonormalBasis.norm_eq_one). Hence every summand of the sum defining |α|² is at most ‖α‖² (strictly increasing I: square the bound, pow_le_pow_left₀ with sq_abs; other I: 0 ≤ ‖α‖²), and the sum has #(Fin n → Fin P) = P^n summands, so it is at most P^n·‖α‖² (Finset.sum_le_sum, Finset.card_univ). Therefore |α| ≤ √(P^n·‖α‖²) = √(P^n)·‖α‖ (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq with ‖α‖ ≥ 0). ∎

Let P, q, U, T₀ and B ≥ 0 be as in the statement: T₀ : TestFormOn U q →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ and |T₀(ω)| ≤ B·C whenever |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
1. (Operator norm vs. coefficient norm.) Let c := √(P^q) ≥ 0. By (C3) of slice_norm, |α| ≤ c·‖α‖ for every q-covector α on ℝ^P.
2. (Sequential continuity at 0.) Let (ω_j) be a sequence in TestFormOn U q with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. By definition there is a compact K (⊆ U) with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for every j such that, for derivative order 0, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 uniformly on K. Let ε > 0 and choose δ > 0 with B·c·δ < ε (e.g. δ := ε/(B·c + 1)). By Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff, for all sufficiently large j and every x ∈ K, dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x) < δ. The limit is iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x = 0 (the zero test form coerces to the zero function), and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), so ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for x ∈ K; by step 1, |ω_j(x)| ≤ c·δ. If x ∉ K then x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and |ω_j(x)| = 0 ≤ c·δ (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Hence the hypothesis with C := c·δ gives |T₀(ω_j)| ≤ B·c·δ < ε for all large j, i.e. T₀(ω_j) → 0 (Metric.tendsto_nhds).
3. (The current.) Step 2 is exactly the field continuous' of GeometricCurrentOn U q (which demands Tendsto (T₀ ∘ ω) atTop (𝓝 0) for every sequence with TestFormOnConverges ω 0). Hence T := ⟨T₀, step 2⟩ ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U q, and T(ω) = T₀(ω) for every ω by definition (rfl).
4. (Mass.) T.mass = T.massOn U = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U q U}. If ω is admissible, then |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, so T(ω) ≤ |T₀(ω)| ≤ B·1 = B and ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal). By sSup_le, T.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B. ∎

Source: steps 9 and 10 of the parent-supplied proof (the boundary formulas ∂([[0,1]]×X) = {1}×X − {0}×X − [[0,1]]×∂X for any Z with ProdChar(X, Z), and the normality estimate M(∂Z) ≤ 2M(X) + M(∂X)). By (∗) of step 7, the family ∂_sψ_s − dφ_s is itself a dt-slice family of dψ on [0,1], and it is used directly in ProdChar. Siblings used: slice_forms (iwl_cr_ci_slice_testForm), horizontal_slices (dph_iprod_horizontal_slices), slice_continuity (dph_iprod_slice_continuity), slice_ext_deriv (dph_iprod_slice_extDeriv) and horizontal_ftc (dph_iprod_horizontal_ftc).

Notation. ℝ^p = Eucl p; cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1} for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^m; ι(v) := cons(0, v) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι∘v := (fun i => ι (v i)) and (e₀, ι∘v) := Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι (v i)) for tuples v; for a q-covector γ on ℝ^p (γ : Covector (Eucl p) q), |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ = (Σ_{I : Fin q → Fin p strictly increasing} γ(b_{I 0}, …, b_{I (q−1)})²)^{1/2} with b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ i, and ‖γ‖ is its operator norm; D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, M := mass; for a test form ω, ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl p) q) x; ∂ := boundary; Dψ(y) := fderiv ℝ ψ y; dω denotes the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ q ω, which is definitionally exteriorDerivative ω = extDeriv ω; a family φ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) is a dt-slice family of η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) on [0,1] if φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v) for all s ∈ [0,1], x, v; ProdChar(X, Z) (X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1})) means Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds for every η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every dt-slice family φ of η on [0,1].

0. (Identification of boundary slices.) If ψ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}), Ψ is the family of horizontal_slices for ψ, and ψ_i ∈ D^q(ℝ^m) satisfies ψ_i(x)(v) = ψ(cons(i,x))(ι∘v) for all x, v (i ∈ {0, 1}), then ψ_i = Ψ(i) (Subtype.ext, funext x, ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext v; both sides equal ψ(cons(i,x))(ι∘v)). Also ∂T(ω) = T(dω) for every current T of positive degree (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), where dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n ω.
1. (Conjunct (II).) Let X ∈ D_0(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, Z ∈ D_{0+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), ψ ∈ D^0(ℝ^{m+1}) and ψ₀, ψ₁ as in (II). horizontal_slices (q := 0) gives Ψ, Ψ′ with Ψ(s)(x)(v) = ψ(cons(s,x))(ι∘v) and Ψ′(s)(x)(v) = Dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀)(ι∘v) for all s, x, v. By (E0) of slice_ext_deriv, Ψ′(s)(x)(v) = dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v) for all s, x, v, so Ψ′ is a dt-slice family of dψ ∈ D^{0+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) on [0,1]. Hence ∂Z(ψ) = Z(dψ) = ∫_0^1 X(Ψ′(s)) ds (ProdChar) = X(Ψ(1)) − X(Ψ(0)) (third conjunct of horizontal_ftc) = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀) (step 0).
2. (Conjunct (III).) Let X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, Z ∈ D_{j+1+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), ψ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ψ₀, ψ₁ as in (III) and φ a dt-slice family of ψ on [0,1]. horizontal_slices (q := j+1) gives Ψ, Ψ′ as in step 1; horizontal_ftc gives (i) continuity of s ↦ X(Ψ′(s)) and (iii) ∫_0^1 X(Ψ′(s)) ds = X(Ψ(1)) − X(Ψ(0)). Define F(s) := Ψ′(s) − dφ(s) ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^m), dφ(s) := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ j (φ(s)).
   (a) F is a dt-slice family of dψ on [0,1]: for s ∈ [0,1], φ(s) satisfies the hypothesis of (E1) of slice_ext_deriv at this s (it is the slice identity of φ at s, for all x, w), so for all x, v: F(s)(x)(v) = Dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀)(ι∘v) − dφ(s)(x)(v) = dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v).
   (b) By ProdChar(X, Z), ∂Z(ψ) = Z(dψ) = ∫_0^1 X(F(s)) ds; by linearity and boundary_apply, X(F(s)) = X(Ψ′(s)) − X(dφ(s)) = X(Ψ′(s)) − ∂X(φ(s)) for every s (in Lean `exact map_sub X.toCurrent _ _`).
   (c) Integrability: s ↦ X(Ψ′(s)) is continuous, hence interval integrable; s ↦ X(F(s)) is continuous on [0,1] by (D1) of slice_continuity applied to dψ and the family F (by (a)); hence s ↦ ∂X(φ(s)) = X(Ψ′(s)) − X(F(s)) is continuous on [0,1] (ContinuousOn.sub, ContinuousOn.congr) and interval integrable on [0,1] (ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable_of_Icc).
   (d) By intervalIntegral.integral_sub, ∂Z(ψ) = ∫_0^1 X(Ψ′(s)) ds − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ(s)) ds = X(Ψ(1)) − X(Ψ(0)) − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ(s)) ds = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀) − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ(s)) ds (step 0).
3. (Conjunct (N): reduction.) Let X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), and assume the HEq-normality hypothesis. M(∂Z) = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal(∂Z(ψ)) : ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ}. It suffices to find A ∈ ℝ with ∂Z(ψ) ≤ A for every admissible ψ: then M(∂Z) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal A < ∞ (sSup_le, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top). Let B := M(X).toReal. Admissible ψ satisfy |ψ(y)| ≤ 1 for all y; ψ is continuous with compact support.
4. (Case k = 0.) For admissible ψ, horizontal_slices gives Ψ, Ψ′, and (II) (step 1) with ψ₀ := Ψ(0), ψ₁ := Ψ(1) gives ∂Z(ψ) = X(Ψ(1)) − X(Ψ(0)). By (D2) of slice_continuity (ω := ψ, C := 1), |X(Ψ(s))| ≤ B for every s. Hence ∂Z(ψ) ≤ 2B; take A := 2B.
5. (Case k = j + 1.) The hypothesis with this j and Y := X (k = j + 1 by rfl, HEq.rfl) gives M(∂X) < ∞; let B′ := M(∂X).toReal. For admissible ψ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), horizontal_slices gives Ψ, Ψ′ and slice_forms (P := m, m := j, η := ψ) gives φ with φ(s)(x)(v) = ψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ι∘v) for all s (in particular a dt-slice family of ψ on [0,1]). By (III) (step 2) with ψ₀ := Ψ(0), ψ₁ := Ψ(1): ∂Z(ψ) = X(Ψ(1)) − X(Ψ(0)) − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ(s)) ds. As in step 4, |X(Ψ(i))| ≤ B. By (D1) of slice_continuity applied to the current ∂X ∈ D_j(ℝ^m) (finite mass), η := ψ, the family φ and C := 1, |∂X(φ(s))| ≤ B′ for s ∈ [0,1]; so |∫_0^1 ∂X(φ(s)) ds| ≤ B′·|1 − 0| = B′ (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const, uIoc 0 1 ⊆ Icc 0 1). Hence ∂Z(ψ) ≤ 2B + B′; take A := 2B + B′. ∎
